[DESCRIPTION]: f(x) ignores the magnitude of x and depends only on its sign. For any negative input it returns the constant -14.96. For any positive input it returns the constant 52.2. For an input exactly equal to zero it returns a very large constant, 898156.8. In other words, it is a sign/step function with three constant branches, taking special (large) behavior at exactly x = 0.

[DOMAIN]: Domain is all real numbers (-inf, inf). There is no special behavior over an interval—only a single special point at x = 0. For all x < 0 the value is -14.96; for all x > 0 the value is 52.2; and exactly at x = 0 the value is 898156.8. The "unexpected" behavior is isolated to the single point x = 0 (no numeric interval, effectively the degenerate interval [0, 0] or a very tiny neighborhood of 0).
